items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I talked to him about Sarah. And he didn't use that kind of language. He just didn't have no eyes for usin' Sarah Vaughan at all. And he had also heard her.

ctx.x: He said, "Oh good! Who's the vocalist?" I said, "I've got a girl named Sarah Vaughan." "Sarah Vaughan? Who is that?" "You remember when I was playing with the Eckstine band last year and we played the Howard Theatre, and you came by, you came backstage to see Billy?" He said, "Yeah, I remember." I said, "Well, it's the girl who sang with the band?" He said, "What? That little black bitch?" He said, "John, I wouldn't hire her singing in my toilet." He said, "Man, bring me a pretty woman. Bring me somebody who look…

But I went on trying to find some work with Sarah, and I went to another club owner who was up at Seventh and T Streets then. There was a club called the Off-Beat, and the guy that was managing it then was a guy named Tassin(?). He's got a place of business here now, I think; I think he has a restaurant and a cleaners. But then he was running a club. And I talked to him about Sarah. And he didn't use that kind of language. He just didn't have no eyes for usin' Sarah Vaughan at all. And he had also heard her.
